page: Microsoft Azure M128s is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor architecture operating at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 2048.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It also includes 4194 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is consistently low, with stress-ng, gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution is robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and bzip3 decompression benchmarks ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, with uncached large-block read and write operations reaching top-tier status in the top 10%.

Given its massive memory footprint and high multi-core throughput, the M128s is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and Redis caching layers, where it achieves strong transaction rates. However, it is poorly suited for single-threaded tasks or text-generation LLM inference. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of RAM and local SSD storage makes it a viable option for consolidating large enterprise databases, though the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a tradeoff in single-threaded efficiency compared to newer hardware classes.
